queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A story of someone who set out to build or win something that was theirs to do, met the first test, and kept going.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
alternates.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
alternates.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
alternates.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
alternates.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Worship of Shiva
prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

alternates.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
alternates.setting: Letter from Alameda, California, 18 April 1900, after laying down his role as leader.
alternates.line: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
alternates.translation: I am glad I was born, glad I suffered so, glad I did make big blunders, glad to enter peace.
alternates.why: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

prasang.title: 'I am drifting': a letter from Alameda (1900)
prasang.summary: Two years before his death, worn out, he writes that he has laid down the role of leader. He is glad he was born, glad he suffered, glad he made big blunders. He admits that ambition, personality, fear and love of power lay behind his work, and says they are fading as he drifts toward peace.
prasang.lesson: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda

verse.line: The greatest religion is to be true to your own nature. Have faith in yourselves!
verse.translation: The greatest religion is to be true to your own nature. Have faith in yourselves!
verse.for_you: You are watching things turn in a good direction, and your family is well. That is your own nature showing up. Keep going with faith in that.
verse.try_today: Notice one small way your nature is showing itself today.
verse.scene_line: You stand in your own truth, as the verse asks.

verse.speaker: Lakshman
verse.setting: At Lake Pampa, Lakshman pulls Ram out of despair after Sita has been taken.
verse.sanskrit: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
verse.line: There is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the one who has it, nothing is out of reach.
verse.translation: Noble brother, enthusiasm is powerful; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the person who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach.
verse.why: Beauty can sharpen grief; a friend can remind you of your own strength.

prasang.title: Grief in springtime at Pampa
prasang.summary: At the beautiful lake of Pampa in spring, everything reminds Ram of Sita and his grief deepens. Lakshman tells him there is no strength greater than enthusiasm, and to rouse himself.
prasang.story_hook: Spring had come to the lake, and every flower made Ram's grief worse.
prasang.lesson: Beauty can sharpen grief; a friend can remind you of your own strength.

verse.for_you: You feel the turn. That steady energy in you is what makes the good direction keep moving. Let it be enough today.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing you are moving toward today and feel the energy in your own hands.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of a good turn, and the world is opening before you.

why: No strength greater than the will to go on (Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha 1.121 (Gita Press))

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Poem 'Hold On Yet a While, Brave Heart', second stanza.
verse.line: No winter was but summer came behind,
verse.translation: No winter was but summer came behind, Each hollow crests the wave, They push each other in light and shade; Be steady then and brave.
verse.why: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

prasang.title: 'Hold on yet a while, brave heart' (poem to the Maharaja of Khetri)
prasang.summary: A short poem of encouragement to a friend. Clouds hide the sun for a while, summer always follows winter, and no honest struggle is wasted even when hopes fail.
prasang.lesson: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

verse.for_you: Your family is well, and the nation is turning toward good. Summer always follows winter. Hold steady and brave.
verse.try_today: Notice the light and shade in your day. Be steady.

verse.speaker: Garuda
verse.setting: Garuda, his doubt resolved, thanks Kakbhushundi.
verse.sanskrit: जो अति आतप ब्याकुल होई। तरु छाया सुख जानइ सोई॥ जौं नहिं होत मोह अति मोही। मिलतेउँ तात कवन बिधि तोही ॥
verse.line: Only the one scorched by the sun knows the shade. Without my doubt, I'd never have found you.
verse.translation: Only one scorched by the sun knows the comfort of a tree's shade. Friend, had I not been so deeply confused, how would I ever have met you?
verse.why: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

prasang.title: Garuda's doubt
prasang.summary: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.
prasang.story_hook: The great eagle Garuda flew to a crow to ask a question.
prasang.lesson: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.

verse.for_you: You sense the turn in your nation and the health of your family. That warmth you feel is real. Let it be your shade today.
verse.try_today: Notice one small comfort this morning and let it settle.

why: the confusion he was ashamed of is seen as the road to what he found

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: The most quoted lines of the graduation address.
verse.sanskrit: देवपितृकार्याभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । मातृदेवो भव । पितृदेवो भव । आचार्यदेवो भव । अतिथिदेवो भव ।
verse.line: Treat your mother as divine, your father as divine, your teacher as divine, your guest as divine.
verse.translation: Do not neglect your duties to the gods and the ancestors. Let your mother be a god to you. Let your father be a god to you. Let your teacher be a god to you. Let your guest be a god to you.
verse.why: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.
verse.misuse: Honouring parents does not mean accepting mistreatment or giving up your own conscience.

prasang.title: The graduation address
prasang.summary: As a student finishes his studies and leaves to start family life, the teacher gives him parting instructions: speak truth, do right, keep learning, honour mother, father, teacher and guest, give with grace. He even tells the student to copy only the teachers' good conduct, and when in doubt to act as thoughtful, gentle people would.
prasang.lesson: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

verse.for_you: Your family is well and the world is turning. In this hopeful moment, see the divine in the ones who raised you and the ones who guide you.
verse.try_today: Notice one person today who has shaped you, and let them feel your quiet gratitude.

why: those who raised and taught you are to be honoured as one honours a deity
the guest and the elder are served as sacred

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: Closing verse of the section praising learning: the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
verse.sanskrit: असन्तो नाभ्यर्थ्याः सुहृदपि न याच्यः कृशधनः प्रिया न्याय्या वृत्तिर्मलिनमसुभङ्गेऽप्यसुकरम् । विपद्युच्चैः स्थेयं पदमनुविधेयं च महतां सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥
verse.line: Don't beg favours from the wicked or money from a struggling friend. Stand tall in hard times.
verse.translation: Do not ask the wicked for favours; do not ask a friend of slender means for money; love a just way of earning; do nothing base even when life is at stake; stand tall in trouble; follow in the footsteps of the great. Who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
verse.why: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.
verse.misuse: 'Even when life is at stake' is the poet's intensity; no principle asks you to harm yourself.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
prasang.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
prasang.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.

verse.for_you: The good direction you sense is not borrowed. You stand tall in your own right. Keep walking your own path with quiet resolve.
verse.try_today: Notice one small choice today that stays just and true to your own standards.
verse.scene_line: You watch your family thrive while the world turns, and you choose your own just way.

story.title: Bharata's fourteen-year wait ends
story.story_hook: For fourteen years Bharata had counted the days; now a stranger was telling him to stop.
story.summary: Hanuman finds Bharata thin, in bark clothes, still waiting. Hearing Ram is near, Bharata faints with joy: a person who stays alive will find joy, even after a hundred years. He places the sandals back on Ram's feet and hands back the kingdom he kept in trust, now ten times richer.
story.lesson: Faithful waiting is rewarded; return what was entrusted to you, and more.
story.hook_title: Bharata had counted the days for fourteen years, and then Hanuman arrived
story.teaser: Bharata had counted the days for fourteen years, and then Hanuman arrived
story.for_you: You are tending what was given to you with care. Now you return it larger and without asking for anything in return. That act of giving back is the fullness of your own life.

why: What is held in trust is to be grown and returned without claim; that completes a life's purpose.
